items.title: No immediate plans to amend laws on overloaded heavy vehicles, says Loke
items.summary: Its minister Anthony Loke said the ministry would focus on firm and consistent enforcement, including action against repeat offenders, to protect road users and reduce road damage. He said the Land Public Transport Agency had strengthened its punitive action matrix for operator offences, allowing it to suspend or revoke vehicle permits and operator licences based on the severity and recurrence of offences. "Action against overloading covers drivers or vehicle owners, depending on the offence committed, as well as operators who breach licence conditions.

items.title: Ismail claims full support of all assemblymen
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim said he had the full support of all 24 Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional assemblymen in leading the state government. He said their support was evident in efforts to ensure the 2027 Negri Sembilan Budget was ready for tabling at the state legislative assembly sitting on Nov 27. All 24 government assemblymen support me.

items.title: Zahid confirms positive outcome in BN-MCA talks over Melaka seats
items.summary: DURIAN TUNGGAL: Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has confirmed that special discussions with MCA leadership over Melaka election seat allocations ended positively. Zahid, who is also deputy prime minister, said the discussions involved MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong, BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir, and Melaka BN chairman and Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh. "The meeting with the MCA president, the Barisan Nasional secretary-general, and the Melaka chief minister showed positive developments.

items.title: Drunk, drug-impaired drivers may be required to compensate victims
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Transport Ministry is proposing amendments to the Road Transport Act to require offenders convicted of driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs to compensate victims or their next of kin. Transport Minister Anthony Loke said Section 426 of the Criminal Procedure Code already provided for compensation, but the proposal would make it an additional punishment alongside fines and imprisonment. "The proposal would cover cases resulting in death, serious injury or permanent disability.

items.title: AME Elite bags RM120mil BAC project
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: AME Elite Consortium Bhd has secured a RM120 million contract to build a manufacturing and testing facility for global cooling solutions provider BAC in Nilai, Negri Sembilan. Its construction arm AME Construction Sdn Bhd received the contract from project owner Rock Link Sdn Bhd to develop a 30,000 sq m facility, which is scheduled for completion within 14 months. The facility will manufacture closed-circuit cooling towers, adiabatic coolers, hybrid systems and liquid cooling solutions.

items.title: Man found drowned in Sungai Petani river
items.summary: Mohamad Solihim Mohd Noor, 38, was found at 8.49am after members of the public reported the discovery, the Kedah Fire and Rescue Department's Operations Centre said. His body was found floating near Kampung Belida Health Clinic, about 6km from the Lesung Fire and Rescue Control Post. Six members of the Sungai Petani Fire and Rescue Station's Water Rescue Team were dispatched to the location.

items.title: EAIC recommends action against Nada officers over raid SOP breaches
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Enforcement Agency Integrity Commission (EAIC) has recommended disciplinary action against National Anti-Drugs Agency (Nada) officers over negligence and breaches of standard operating procedures (SOPs) during a raid in Bera, Pahang. "The investigation found negligence in the tactical handling of the raid and non-compliance with SOPs by the Bera Nada operations team, which triggered panic and a scuffle resulting in injuries to a civilian or third party at the scene," the commission said. The investigation, conducted under Section 27(4) of the Enforcement Agency Integrity Commission Act, also found that officers from the Bera Nada office had breached the agency director-general's standing orders, specifically PTKP BAB 02/2025 (Amendment 2026).

items.title: EC to meet on Nov 6 to set key dates for Sarawak polls
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Election Commission (EC) will hold a special meeting on Nov 6 to discuss key dates for the 13th Sarawak state election. He said the EC had today received official notification from Sarawak State Legislative Assembly Speaker Tan Sri Mohamad Asfia Awang Nassar confirming the dissolution of the 19th Sarawak State Legislative Assembly, effective yesterday, in accordance with Article 21(2) of the State Constitution. "Under Article 21(4) of the Sarawak State Constitution, an election must be held within 60 days of the dissolution," he said.

items.title: Negri Sembilan to remain without exco until court ruling, says MB
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has no plans to propose new state executive council (Exco) members until the dispute over their appointments is resolved in court. He said the state government was currently operating without an exco line-up. Ismail was responding to questions about the state administration's lack of exco members and claims that some of the former exco members might withdraw their court application.

items.title: Nik Nazmi spends over 3 hours giving statement to JAIS over khalwat case
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Former Setiawangsa member of parliament Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad today completed the recording of his statement with the Selangor Islamic Religious Department over a khalwat (close proximity) case. His Syariah lawyer, Muhammad Amirul Ashraf A. Ghani, said Nik Nazmi had appeared before Jais to assist in investigations under Section 29 of the Syariah Criminal Offences (Selangor) Enactment 1995. Nik Nazmi, 44, arrived at the Jais office at about 9.15am and left at 1.30pm.

items.title: Transport Ministry plans jail terms for rail cable thieves
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Transport Ministry plans to amend the Land Public Transport Act to impose heavier penalties, including jail terms, on those who steal cables from rail infrastructure. "The Transport Ministry is taking steps to amend the Land Public Transport Act to increase penalties for cable theft, including imprisonment. Earlier, Datuk Dr Radzi Jidin (PN-Putrajaya) raised concerns over cable theft involving public transport infrastructure.

items.title: Northeast monsoon begins, raising flood risks in low-lying areas
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Low-lying areas along the peninsula's west coast face flood risks as the northeast monsoon begins today, with residents urged to heed weather warnings. Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM) International Strategic and Sustainable Development Goals Consultancy Centre principal fellow Professor Dr Mohd Ekhwan Toriman said recent heavy rain had affected several areas, including Yan, Kuala Muda and Pendang in Kedah, as well as low-lying areas in Penang and Penampang, Sabah. He said the northeast monsoon, expected to last until March next year, would bring strong winds, prolonged rain and rising sea levels along coastal areas.

items.title: Health Service Commission bill targeted for tabling before end of 15th Parliament - Dzulkefly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Ministry of Health (MOH) aims to obtain a policy decision from the Cabinet on the establishment of the Health Service Commission this year and, if approved, table the Bill in Parliament by the end of the 15th Parliament at the latest. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the establishment of the commission would further strengthen the management of human resources and the welfare of healthcare personnel, covering all 86 service schemes under the MOH. "These are among our efforts to improve matters while moving towards the establishment of a Health Service Commission, as envisaged in the White Paper by the Health Reform Commission," he said.

items.title: Saifuddin quips he is 'envious' of Ngeh's vast Kelantan plantations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail quipped that he was "envious" of Beruas member of parliament Datuk Ngeh Koo Ham's extensive plantations in Kelantan. Ngeh said the cumbersome application process, which includes travelling to Putrajaya for interviews, had driven some employers to hire undocumented foreign workers. "Undocumented migrants would not come if employers could hire and pay foreign workers legally," he said.

items.title: Impact Capital sets 22 sen IPO price
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Impact Capital Holdings Bhd expects to raise RM21.27 million from its initial public offering (IPO) ahead of its planned listing on the ACE Market of Bursa Malaysia on Nov 24. The information and communications technology (ICT) systems integrator's IPO comprises a public issue of 96.69 million new shares and an offer for sale of 28.62 million existing shares, at an issue price of 22 sen per share. The company has allocated RM5.17 million for working capital and RM4.8 million for estimated listing expenses.

items.title: Indonesia deploys 'oxygen bus' as forest-fire haze chokes residents
items.summary: PALANGKA RAYA, Indonesia: A bus fitted out with oxygen tanks is providing a sanctuary in a city on Indonesia's Borneo island where people are choking from forest-fire-induced haze and the blazes show no sign of letting up. As respiratory illnesses increased in the Central Kalimantan city of Palangka Raya, the local government provided an 'oxygen bus' replete with oxygen tanks and medical professionals who offer residents a chance to be hooked up to a small oxygen tube around their nose for 5 to 10 minutes at a time. "The service is intended to help people access oxygen, particularly those experiencing respiratory problems or who need oxygen support amid unhealthy air quality conditions," the Central Kalimantan provincial health department said on Instagram this week.

items.title: Man charged with flashing private parts to 12-year-old girl in condominium lift
items.summary: Muhammad Aniq Mohd Jafri, 25, is accused of committing the offence at a condominium in Taman Danau Desa between 6.30pm and 6.50pm on April 1. Aniq entered his plea before judge Suhaila Haron. Deputy public prosecutor V. Suloshani sought bail of RM10,000 with one surety and asked the court to impound the accused's passport and require him to report to a police station monthly.

items.title: Four foreign boys detained over intimidation of 71-year-old woman
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM: Four foreign boys aged between nine and 12 have been detained following a criminal intimidation report lodged by a 71-year-old woman in Taman Sri Rambai. Seberang Prai Tengah district police chief Assistant Commissioner Nik Aminuddin Raja Abdullah said police received the report yesterday over an incident outside the woman's home on Oct 22 at 6pm. Following investigations, police detained the four boys in separate operations around Taman Sri Rambai and seized several items believed to be linked to the incident.

items.title: Dr Siti Hawa's mother recalls final days of SMA scholar who defied odds
items.summary: KUANTAN: Dr Siti Hawa Apandi, the country's first spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) patient to complete four levels of higher education at a single university, spent much of her final days resting in bed. Her mother, Zaidah Tamjis, 64, said Siti Hawa, 37, had been resting more than usual at their home in Taman Seri Mahkota Aman here, instead of following her routine of sitting for long periods while using her laptop. In August, Siti Hawa was recognised by the Malaysia Book of Records for completing her diploma, bachelor's degree, master's degree and PhD at Universiti Malaysia Pahang Al-Sultan Abdullah (UMPSA).

items.title: [UPDATED] Penang holds developer, landowner responsible for fatal landslide, warns of legal action
items.summary: Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow warned of possible legal consequences, saying the landslide occurred on the developer's land and that the parties were responsible for site safety and mitigation measures. "The landowner and developer must take responsibility for the effects of the landslide, including legal implications, approval-related matters and mitigation works to restore site safety," he said when met at the scene. On possible legal action, Chow said affected parties were entitled to pursue legal remedies against those responsible.

items.title: EV sales are picking up, but is the after sales support ready to service the market?
items.summary: GIVEN the current sales trend of the Proton e.MAS brand, which clocked just over 32,000 sales in 2026, it looks like electrified vehicles have gained enough traction to break the 10 per cent barrier sometime in the final quarter of this year. This point typically sits around 12 to 15 per cent of total market volume. Globally, battery electric vehicles (BEV) crossed that threshold some three years ago.

items.title: Fix your water supply before chasing RM720b GDP dream, Akmal tells SG4 states
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — Chronic deficits in basic utilities, highlighted by Kedah's zero per cent water reserve margin, will derail the ambitious long-term economic targets set by the four opposition-led SG4 states, Economy Minister Akmal Nasir warned today. Federal development expenditure in the four states reached RM7.70 billion in 2025, approximately 6.8 times their combined state development allocations of roughly RM1.13 billion. Addressing commercial inflows, Akmal cited Malaysian Investment Development Authority data recording RM37.23 billion in approved investments and 18,319 potential jobs across the four states in 2025.

items.title: Dzulkefly: Health Service Commission Bill to be tabled by end of 15th Parliament if approved
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) aims to obtain a policy decision from the Cabinet on the establishment of the Health Service Commission (SPK) this year and, if approved, table the Bill in Parliament by the end of the 15th Parliament at the latest. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the establishment of the commission would further strengthen the management of human resources and the welfare of healthcare personnel, covering all 86 service schemes under the MOH. “These are among our efforts to improve matters while moving towards the establishment of a Health Service Commission, as envisaged in the White Paper by the Health Reform Commission,” he said.

items.title: MASFIH wants federal aid for families of 54 missing Malaysians
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Solidarity Families in Hope (MASFIH) wants the government to provide humanitarian aid to families of 54 Malaysians missing in Nepal and appoint Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan to coordinate assistance. He said several ministers had responded positively. Manivannan said families were struggling to obtain essential financial information and manage their missing relatives' financial obligations because they could not obtain the usual consent or authorisation.

items.title: Govt initiates legal action against Zetrix AI over unpaid JPJ revenue, rejected RM231m cheque
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The government is taking civil legal action against collection agent Zetrix AI Berhad after the company failed to remit millions in government revenue collected on behalf of the Road Transport Department (JPJ). Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the legal action followed the company’s failure to settle its total outstanding balance and accrued late-payment penalties within the stipulated deadline. JPJ subsequently lodged a police report on October 7 over the unremitted government revenue.

items.title: RM14.3mil returned to online scam victims
items.summary: However, he said the amount recovered remained insufficient given the substantial losses suffered by scam victims. From Oct 12, 2022 to August this year, the NSRC's 997 hotline received 468,675 calls involving reported losses totalling RM1.2 billion, he said. Saifuddin said police had intensified intelligence gathering and enforcement operations against online scam syndicates.

items.title: US midterms: 470 seats up for grabs in US$12bil election battle
items.summary: A Democratic takeover of either chamber would constrain Trump's agenda and bring greater congressional scrutiny of his administration; Republican victories would preserve the party's control in Washington. 3: The net number of seats Democrats need to gain to take control. In 2024, Republicans won a 220-215 majority, although deaths, resignations and a party switch mean the current House stands at 218 Republicans, 214 Democrats, one independent and two vacancies.

items.title: Saifuddin: No cover-up in death of man in police custody
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: There has been no attempt to cover up the case of Noorizwan Zulkefly, who died in police custody, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. "The Home Ministry has never compromised on any violations. Also present were Pasir Gudang member of paliament (MP) Hassan Abdul Karim, Jelutong MP RSN Rayer, Bentong MP Young Syefura Othman, Bukit Bendera MP Syerleena Abdul Rashid and Beruas MP Datuk Ngeh Koo Ham.

items.title: Singapore to update solar roadmap to meet 4GWp target by 2035
items.summary: SINGAPORE, Oct 27 — Singapore will update its Solar Photovoltaic (PV) Roadmap to support its new target of deploying 4 gigawatt-peak (GWp) of solar capacity by 2035, the Energy Market Authority (EMA) said. EMA said it would collaborate with the Solar Energy Research Institute of Singapore (SERIS) to refresh the roadmap, which was last updated in 2020. EMA is also taking steps to encourage greater solar adoption for private residential landed properties to unlock more opportunities for solar deployment.

items.title: Wan Saiful accuses Bersatu of being 'Trojan horse' within PN
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Datuk Wan Saiful Wan Jan has accused Bersatu of being a "Trojan horse" within Perikatan Nasional (PN) and called for disciplinary action against the party. The Parti Wawasan Negara vice-president also accused Bersatu secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali of echoing DAP's narrative by suggesting that Pas was incapable of managing the coalition. Wan Saiful claimed that Azmin and Bersatu were advancing DAP's agenda by spreading what he described as false propaganda about Pas' leadership of PN.

items.title: Japan rape trial of ex-senior prosecutor resumes after two-year pause
items.summary: TOKYO: The trial of a Japanese former senior prosecutor accused of rape in one of the country's most high-profile cases of alleged sexual assault restarted on Tuesday after a two-year pause. Few women in Japan speak out about sexual assault, but a former prosecutor, who uses the pseudonym Hikari, came forward in 2024 to accuse her boss of raping her six years earlier. The trial first began in October 2024 but was halted after Kentaro Kitagawa – who served as head of the Osaka District Public Prosecutor's Office at the time of the alleged rape – withdrew his initial admission of guilt and said the sex was consensual.

items.title: Maybank Islamic, CGC launch first supply chain financing guarantee scheme
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Maybank Islamic Bhd has teamed up with Credit Guarantee Corporation Malaysia Bhd (CGC) to introduce Malaysia's first supply chain financing guarantee scheme anchored by mid-tier companies (MTCs). Under the collaboration, Maybank Islamic will provide Syariah-compliant supply chain financing facilities, while CGC will extend guarantee support to eligible MTCs under its BizJamin-i Mid-Tier Companies scheme. One of the key features is CGC's guarantee support, which enables eligible MTCs to act as anchors in their supply chains, allowing their suppliers to access financing against approved invoices.

items.title: Johor man with six previous criminal and drug-related offences arrested over axe murder of 68-year-old Felda settler
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Oct 27 — Police arrested a 41-year-old man suspected of hacking a settler to death with an axe at Felda Lok Heng Selatan last night. Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the suspect was arrested by a joint team from the state contingent and district police at a palm oil plantation here at 10.26am today. “Police seized a motorcycle and an axe from the suspect.

items.title: ‘Betrayal’: Putrajaya cuts off Penang petrol station over suspected Budi Madani subsidy abuse
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — Putrajaya has cut off a petrol station in Sungai Buaya, Nibong Tebal, Penang, from the Budi Madani fuel subsidy over suspected misuse that allegedly involved customers’ MyKad details being used without their knowledge. It has barred the station from selling subsidised RON95 and diesel under Budi Madani. It did not name the petrol station.

items.title: Mahathir weighs next move on Dec 4 in RM150mil Anwar defamation suit
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad will inform the High Court on Dec 4 how he intends to proceed with his RM150 million defamation suit against Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Dr Mahathir's lawyer, Muhammad Rafique Rashid Ali, said he had asked the court to give his client time to decide how to proceed in view of his current condition. "We are all aware of Dr Mahathir's condition.

items.title: MBPP advised project consultant on slope safety months before fatal landslide
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) had advised the consultant for the development project linked to Sunday's fatal landslide to take slope safety precautions in August. Mayor Datuk A. Rajendran said the council had advised the project consultant following a site visit that month. The development project was issued a stop-work order following Sunday's landslide.

items.title: Nik Nazmi spends four hours at Jais, now waits to hear if he will be charged
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 27 — Bersama co-founder Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad spent more than four hours at the Selangor Islamic Religious Department here today, giving his statement over the khalwat case. That decision, he said, rests with the Selangor Syariah Prosecution Department. He said statements from Nik Nazmi and the woman linked to the case were taken separately.

items.title: LPT3 highway from Terengganu to Kelantan to proceed via competitive bidding, says Nanta
items.summary: Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said the proposed alignment, stretching from Kampung Gemuruh in Terengganu to Tunjong in Kelantan, would complement LPT1 and LPT2 in connecting Pahang, Terengganu and Kelantan. Nanta said the government’s current priority was to ensure that the Central Spine Road (LTU) and Kota Bharu-Kuala Krai Highway (KBKK) projects progressed smoothly and were completed on schedule. For the 70.4-kilometre KBKK project, he said overall physical progress had reached 78.80 per cent, with the Pasir Hor-Kadok stretch fully completed.

items.title: Pahang allocates RM3.78m for monsoon preparations, sends aid supplies to 167 forward bases
items.summary: KUANTAN, Oct 27 — The Pahang state government has allocated more than RM3 million to prepare for the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon (MTL), including the early delivery of aid supplies to 167 forward bases statewide. Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail said the state government, through the Pahang Social Welfare Department (JKM), had coordinated a total allocation of RM3,785,115.30 for dry food supplies, logistics, transportation and labour costs across 11 districts. He said 332,906 units of dry food supplies, comprising nine basic food items weighing a total of 225.11 tonnes, would be distributed to the forward bases from today until Nov 14.

items.title: Crocodile snatches 13-year-old in Sarawak, rescue teams launch search
items.summary: The Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba) said it was notified of the incident at around 7pm. Bomba Sarawak said Simunjan fire station personnel are currently at the scene conducting a search and rescue (SAR) operation for the boy. In a Facebook post, licensed crocodile hunters Sarawak Crocter said the attack occurred at around 4pm when the victim was loading oil palm fruits into a boat.

items.title: Nearly 72pc of major hospitals record bed waiting times under eight hours, says Dzulkefly
items.summary: As of June 2026, 28 of the country’s 39 Type 1 and Type 2 hospitals, or 71.8 per cent, recorded average waiting times of less than eight hours for admission from Emergency Departments. These hospitals include state hospitals and major specialist hospitals that handle high numbers of emergency patients and referrals from surrounding districts. Dzulkefly added that 94 of 103 Type 3 and Type 4 hospitals (91.3 per cent), including minor specialist hospitals and hospitals without specialists, had average bed waiting times under four hours.

items.title: Ramanan: More funding being considered for Uyarvu Madani to help small Indian entrepreneurs
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 27 — The government, through the Malaysian Indian Transformation Unit (MITRA), will consider applying for additional funding to expand assistance to small entrepreneurs, particularly those in the B40 and M40 groups who are in need, through the Uyarvu Madani programme following the extraordinary response to applications for the programme. Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the government will also examine other sources of financing, including collaboration through other agencies, to help more entrepreneurs expand their businesses. “We received 8,368 applications for Uyarvu Madani, but we can only grant it to about 780 recipients.

items.title: MMEA officer killed, two injured during operation in Kuala Perlis waters
items.summary: Kangar district police chief ACP Yusharifuddin Mohd Yusop, when contacted by Bernama, confirmed that the incident occurred yesterday at around 11 pm, however, he said that further information regarding the incident can only be released by the MMEA. “I can only confirm receiving the report of this incident, but further information regarding this incident can only be released by the MMEA,” he said. — Bernama

items.title: Sarawak Assembly dissolution notification sent to EC, says Speaker
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 27 — A notification letter on the dissolution of the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly has been sent to the Election Commission (EC) today, said Speaker Tan Sri Mohamad Asfia Awang Nassar. He said he had received the declaration of the dissolution of the state assemby, signed by Sarawak Governor Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar on Friday (Oct 23) “The declaration of dissolution is also in accordance with Article 21(2) of the State Constitution, which empowers the Governor of Sarawak to dissolve the state assembly. On Oct 23, Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg announced that the State Legislative Assembly would be dissolved on Monday (Oct 26), paving the way for the 13th state election.

items.title: Anwar defends bigger development allocations for Sabah, Sarawak, cites infrastructure needs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The government has defended its decision to provide larger development allocations for Sabah and Sarawak, citing their geographical challenges and infrastructure needs. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said these needs included the poor condition of roads in several areas of Sabah, despite its smaller population compared with other states. In response, Anwar said the development allocations for Sabah and Sarawak announced in Budget 2027 did not include expenditure for the projects under KKDW raised by the MP.

items.title: Anwar calls for stricter rules for GLCs, says bosses must not treat them as family property
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The government is considering a Government-Owned Entities Bill to tighten governance at government-linked companies (GLCs) and related agencies, and prevent misappropriation such as that seen in 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB), Felda and Tabung Haji. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the proposed law would set clearer rules and ensure government-owned entities, including their subsidiaries, were subject to effective oversight. Instead, investment decisions must be made by investment bodies comprising professionals and people with relevant expertise, he said.

items.title: Anwar plans new law for GLCs and GLICs, cites Battersea losses and eFishery failure
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The government plans to introduce legislation to tighten governance at government-linked companies (GLCs) and government-linked investment companies (GLICs), Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar said clear rules were also needed for subsidiaries of government agencies, adding that the government had not identified governance breaches on the scale previously seen at 1MDB and Tabung Haji. Anwar said investments by GLICs and GLCs helped local companies expand and attract private investment from domestic and foreign investors.

items.title: RM1,000 per attack? Perak police arrest three teens over arson, paint-splashing cases across four states
items.summary: Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said Taiping police arrested the three men at separate locations in Penang between 5pm and 9pm on October 22, and had helped solve nine vandalism cases across four states: two in Perak, three in Kedah, two in Johor, one in Penang and one in Selangor. “The second suspect, a storekeeper, was arrested in Taman Sri Rambai, Bukit Mertajam, where police seized a mobile phone, clothing and a white Nissan Teana. Police are investigating two cases in Taiping.

items.title: Love is in the air, and so is the bill: 13pc of Malaysian men willing to go into debt for dates
items.summary: According to research by Legasi Research, men continue to shoulder most dating expenses, with 59.3 per cent saying they usually pay the entire bill, compared with just 8.2 per cent of women. Dinner dates and the price of romance Shopping malls remain a popular dating destination, with 44.1 per cent of respondents saying they frequent them, while 42.8 per cent opt for cafes or restaurants. Men also appear more likely to feel the financial strain, with 27.5 per cent reporting pressure from dating expenses, compared with 16.4 per cent of women.

items.title: Transferred Perak principal now under police probe after mother reports alleged sexual harassment of her Form Three daughter
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 27 — Police are investigating alleged sexual harassment involving a school principal and a Form Three student in Hutan Melintang, Perak, following a report by the student’s mother. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the report was lodged on October 24, with the case being investigated under Section 15(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017. “Following the report lodged by the victim’s mother, the case is being investigated under Section 15(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017,” he told a press conference at the Perak Police Headquarters today.

items.title: Anwar defends GLIC-funded housing, says Petronas helped develop Putrajaya
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today defended the use of government-linked investment companies (GLICs) to fund domestic development, citing Petronas’ role in Putrajaya and arguing that public needs can be balanced with commercial returns. Anwar, who is also finance minister, said that the national oil company had helped fund Putrajaya’s development through Putrajaya Holdings, which encompasses government offices, public amenities, hotels, commercial ventures and tourism facilities. Anwar said the first phase of a student accommodation initiative would involve 10,000 units, with a longer-term target of 30,000 units involving GLICs.

items.title: Fake hospital calls, bogus investments and loan scams: Police arrest 36 in Perak
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 27 — Perak police have busted three scam syndicates targeting Malaysian, Chinese and Japanese victims in separate raids in Ipoh and Kampar, arresting 36 people. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said five Japanese men, aged 21 to 27, were arrested at a two-storey house in Kampung Simee at about 6.10pm on October 26 for allegedly impersonating staff from a Japanese hospital. Police seized 16 mobile phones, seven iPads and two routers worth RM22,500.

items.title: Buy low, sell high: Kelantan shoppers see opportunity as gold falls to RM503
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Oct 27 — Shoppers have been streaming into Kelantan’s gold shops to snap up jewellery as prices sag to about RM503 a gramme yesterday, the New Straits Times reported today. Many shops around Pasar Siti Khadijah in the Kelantan capital here were crowded with customers, with gold priced between RM503 and RM504 a gramme, according to the newspaper. Gold is deeply rooted in Kelantan, where women have long treated it as both savings and business capital, with monthly sales in the state estimated at about 500kg, the New Straits Times reported previously.

items.title: Lorry driver claims microsleep caused crash that injured two journalists in Perak
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 27 — The lorry driver involved in an accident with two journalists in Menglembu last Sunday claimed that he had experienced a microsleep, which led to the crash, police said. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said police were continuing their investigation. “The lorry driver has given a statement.

items.title: Adam Adli: Pakatan not fielding ‘token candidate’ in Paya Rumput, banking on Azman’s experience
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 27 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is banking on the extensive federal administrative experience of its candidate, Datuk Azman Abidin, in the contest for the Paya Rumput seat in the Melaka state election, said acting Melaka PKR chief Adam Adli Abd Halim. “Paya Rumput is not a place for a token candidate. He said these strengths could help Azman champion the needs of Paya Rumput residents more effectively, particularly in areas involving basic infrastructure development, welfare and community development.

items.title: Heavy rain, high tides put Pulau Perhentian villagers on alert as monsoon season begins
items.summary: JERTIH, Oct 27 — Residents in the village on Pulau Perhentian here have started making early preparations for the Northeast Monsoon (MTL), which is expected to bring heavy rain and pose a flood risk to low-lying areas of the village. Resident Azizah Ab Rahman, 59, said the village was also vulnerable to flooding, especially when heavy rain coincided with high tides, causing water to stagnate and making it difficult for it to drain into the sea. Pulau Perhentian Village Development and Security Committee (JPKK) chairman Nik Zawawi Mohd Nor said about 30 houses were usually affected whenever flooding occurred in the village.

items.title: Caretaker mode: What Sarawak’s government can and can’t do
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 27 — With the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly (DUN) officially dissolved on Monday (Oct 26), the state government remains in office in a caretaker capacity. Three legal experts explain the caretaker government’s role, powers and limitations. Does Sarawak still have a state government after the DUN is dissolved?

items.title: Locked out over maintenance fees? Court says JMBs can’t do that
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 27 — Joint management bodies (JMBs) cannot bar owners from their own units over unpaid maintenance charges, the Court of Appeal has ruled, news outlet Free Malaysia Today reported. The ruling came in an appeal by SL Land Sdn Bhd and Foong Wei Ching against the JMB managing the Sentral Bazar shopping mall in Nilai, Negeri Sembilan, which had refused to let the company’s directors and authorised agents into their units. The court set aside a High Court ruling that had upheld the JMB’s power to impose conditions on entry by defaulters under the Strata Management (Maintenance and Management) Regulations 2015.

items.title: Zahid urges public to stay alert as northeast monsoon begins today
items.summary: He said the monsoon, expected to persist until March 2027, could bring prolonged heavy rainfall, flooding and rough seas, threatening residents’ safety, particularly in vulnerable areas. “This could increase the risk of flooding, particularly in areas near rivers and low-lying areas,” he said in a Facebook post today. Ahmad Zahid said strong winds during the period could also cause rough seas and rising sea levels in the South China Sea.

items.title: Waze alternatives? Delivery riders, e-hailing drivers wait for TuJu to prove itself
items.summary: Muhammad Nabil Khairuddin, 30, a Grab rider, said he first learnt about TuJu through TikTok and Facebook yesterday and was considering downloading it to see how it compared with established navigation apps. For deliveries, however, Nabil said he already relied on Grab’s in-house navigation system, which allows him to find destinations without leaving the ride-hailing app. He said Grab previously allowed riders to choose between Waze and Google Maps, but its own navigation system now offered a more convenient option.
